subject.title: fix(runtime): cancelled workflows no longer continue external commands

question: Should Lobster permanently consume workflow resume and approval capabilities after cancellation once workflow execution has begun, while preserving them for cancellation during setup?
rationale: Both retryability and replay prevention are plausible user expectations; the patch implements a careful boundary, but selecting that permanent runtime contract requires maintainer intent rather than another mechanical code change.

options.title: Adopt post-start consumption
options.body: Accept the PR's explicit boundary: setup-time cancellation remains retryable, while cancellation after execution begins removes the resolved resume capability to prevent replay.

options.title: Preserve broader retryability
options.body: Require a revised contract that retains resumed state after some post-start cancellations, with a new mechanism to prevent replaying already-completed side effects.

recommendation.title: Adopt post-start consumption
recommendation.body: Accept the PR's explicit boundary: setup-time cancellation remains retryable, while cancellation after execution begins removes the resolved resume capability to prevent replay.

likelyOwner.reason: This is a cross-runtime product contract affecting cancellation semantics and durable resume behavior, not a contributor-follow-up defect.
